summary.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.7% YoY to INR137.6 crore, with EBITDA up 43.7% to INR20.9 crore and margin at 15.2%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR137.6 crore against INR117.9 crore a year earlier, up 16.7% YoY. EBITDA rose 43.7% to INR20.9 crore, with margin expanding 286 bps to 15.2%, and PAT rose 83% to INR10.7 crore (7.8% margin). Management attributed the sequential revenue moderation to the US-Iran war and a fuel and gas supply crisis in March-April, which it says is now largely resolved. The consolidated order book stood at about INR1,692 crore as of August 11, 2026, with INR1,526 crore at OFPL wagons and INR166 crore in coach interiors. Management also laid out smart wagon, next-gen wagon, wagon leasing and JV initiatives.

segments.name: Freight wagons (Oriental Foundry Pvt Ltd, OFPL)
segments.commentary: About 75% of consolidated revenue and about INR106 crore in Q1; management guides wagon volumes up more than 45-50% YoY on better capacity utilisation. Installed capacity is 2,400 wagons per annum, with FY26 utilisation around 50%.

segments.name: Seats and berths (rolling stock interiors, ORIL)
segments.commentary: About 16% of revenue; the business holds over 30% market share with installed capacity of about 3,600 coaches per annum. Management expects other businesses to grow 8-10%.

segments.name: Rexine upholstery (ORVIN)
segments.commentary: About 5% of revenue; in-house capacity is 36 lakh meters per annum serving railway and non-railway users.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 wagon dispatches of about 500 vs roughly 300 plus in Q1; FY27 turnover expected at around INR700 crore.
Order book execution at about 200 wagons per month from Q3 FY27 (October-December), which management says fully uses the 2,400-wagon capacity.
Medium-term EBITDA margin targets: 15-17% for freight wagons and 13-15% for rolling stock interiors; consolidated FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 15-17%.
Capacity expansion: application by Q1 FY28; target of 3,600 then 4,800 wagons over 12-18 months from FY28; capex of about INR60-70 crore for the 2,400 to 3,600 step.
No order inflow targeted in FY27; order inflow of about INR600 crore expected in Q1 FY28 (management said FY27 in the call, then corrected to FY28).
capex_capacity: Wagon capacity 2,400 per annum at OFPL, around 50% utilised in FY26; more than 4,000 wagons delivered to date.
Expansion to 3,600 wagons (capex INR60-70 crore), then 4,800 wagons over 12-18 months from FY28, with capacity applications starting Q1 FY28.
Dedicated smart wagon component facility planned in North India by end FY28.
Four manufacturing facilities across 100 acres; in-house bogies, draft gears, springs, couplers and side bearers. Spring plant became operational in FY26.
demand_pricing: Wagon realisation about INR40 lakh per wagon (plus or minus 5%).
Wagon price escalation clause linked to steel WPI, labour index and other commodity indices; management says it does not cover vendor-driven component price hikes.
Management says FY26 and FY25 weakness was due to railway wheel shortages and reliance on external component suppliers, which squeezed margins.
Smart wagon monitoring system priced at about INR2.5-3 lakh per unit; target 30,000 units per annum, implying about INR750 crore revenue (management estimates a INR10,000 crore market).
Freight wagon market expected to nearly double to INR25,000-30,000 crore by 2031; National Rail Plan 2030 targets wagon fleet growth from about 4 lakh to 6 lakh.
Management expects 'at least two or three players' in smart wagons and says competition is anticipated.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for sequential revenue moderation and Q2 run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 to the US-Iran war and the fuel and gas supply crisis in March-April, now largely resolved. Q2 is running faster, with about 500 wagons expected versus roughly 300 plus in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How many wagons does the INR1,526 crore OFPL order book represent and what is the execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3,800 wagons, executed at about 200 wagons per month from Q3 FY27 (October-December).

qa_highlights.question: Capacity expansion plans and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is to go from 2,400 to 3,600 (capex INR60-70 crore), then 4,800 over 12-18 months from FY28; the capacity application is planned for Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did freight revenue not grow in FY25-FY26 (INR458 crore to INR409 crore), and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a railway wheel shortage that restricted supply and underutilised capacity. Backward integration into springs, draft gears and couplers has since stabilised supply.

qa_highlights.question: Debt, cash flow and leverage outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flow should improve with utilisation and debt will reduce, but declined to give FY27/FY28 debt or debt-to-equity figures.

qa_highlights.question: Order inflow pipeline for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 order additions targeted; management expects about INR600 crore of inflow in Q1 FY28. Government wagon tenders are typically clubbed for about two years.

risks_watch: Execution ramp: the plan requires about 200 wagons per month from October 2026 versus about 300 plus in Q1 total; a slip would hit the INR700 crore FY27 target.
Order book inflow is lumpy and tender-driven; no FY27 inflow is targeted and the next inflow of about INR600 crore is pencilled for Q1 FY28.
Smart wagon (HUM JV) timing has slipped: the earlier expected date was June 10 and the tender financial bids are now expected end August; revenue is guided from FY28-29.
Working capital and debt: management gave no debt or D/E figures and said operating cash flow was absent in FY25-FY26.
Input cost exposure to vendor-supplied components not covered by the price variation clause; competition expected in smart wagons.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term freight demand and capacity utilisation, but cautious and evasive on specifics. Management declined to give debt, D/E, growth-CAGR and pipeline figures beyond broad statements, and several answers were unclear due to line quality.

key_quotes: The first quarter of the financial year has been affected by the US -Iran war and, the immediate crisis of the fuel and gas supply which was existing during March and April which is now more or less solved out or under total control.
We hope to do around 500 wagons in the quarter as compared to 300 and odd wagons in the first quarter.
We project to execute at the rate of 200 wagons per month from quarter three of the present financial year.

The squeeze in margin during the period was only because of being dependent on outside suppliers, and during this period even the because of the large order released for the wagons, the prices in the industry were volatile, it was almost like a sellers mar ket, which is again now we are not dependent on it because of our entire backward integration.
For FY27 we are not very keen and not pursuing any addition of the order book because we are totally focused on executing the orders which are on hand.
